definition: A young man who pursues casual sex without emotional commitment, often through manipulation or false romantic signaling.
notes: Emerged c. 2014 in internet and hip-hop culture; the 'fuck' prefix marks crudeness; carries social condemnation but is occasionally used aspirationally in certain subcultures.

definition: Abbreviated form of 'fuckboy'; a young man who uses women for sexual gratification without emotional commitment.
notes: Cleaned-up spelling used on platforms that filter 'fuckboy'; popularized by the HBO Max reality show FBoy Island (2021); primarily Gen Z usage.

definition: A male sex worker or paid male companion, especially one financially kept by an older wealthy woman.
notes: French loanword; retains a glamorized, Old World connotation absent from female equivalents; covers both paid escort and kept-man meanings simultaneously.

definition: A person, typically male, who maintains multiple simultaneous romantic or sexual relationships through charm and deliberate non-commitment.
notes: Rooted in African American vernacular English; peaked in 1990s R&B and hip-hop culture; valence is ambivalent—admiring or critical depending on speaker and context.

definition: A man who systematically studies and applies psychological and social techniques to seduce women, typically for casual sex.
notes: Abbreviated PUA; associated with the seduction community and later red-pill subcultures; popularized by Neil Strauss's The Game (2005) and MTV's The Pickup Artist (2007).

definition: A person, typically male, who is persistently or compulsively driven by sexual desire.
notes: Compound of 'horny' and 'dog'; the dog component implies animal-like lack of restraint and low social status; primarily American English.

definition: A lecherous man; someone who makes persistent unwanted sexual advances or who is indiscreetly and obsessively driven by lust.
notes: Clipped from 'lecher' or 'lecherous'; more common in British English; also functions as a verb ('to lech after someone'); alternate spelling 'letch' exists.

definition: An older man perceived as inappropriately or predatorily interested in sex, especially toward younger people.
notes: The 'dirty' component evokes moral pollution from sexuality; originally framed as a comic archetype, increasingly coded as predatory in post-#MeToo discourse; abbreviated DOM in some online contexts.

definition: A pervert; a person whose sexual interests or behaviors are perceived as deviant, predatory, or grossly inappropriate.
notes: Clipped form of 'pervert'; applied across a wide spectrum from harmless kink-shaming to serious predation; context-dependent severity; also used as a verb.

definition: A person who makes others uncomfortable through unwanted sexual attention, boundary violations, or generally unsettling behavior.
notes: Not exclusively sexual—applies to general unsettling behavior—but its dominant use is sexual/romantic; 'creepiness' has been studied academically (McAndrew & Koehnke, 2016); gender-neutral term applied predominantly to men in practice.

definition: A person who uses power, manipulation, or coercion to obtain sex from unwilling or unable-to-consent victims.
notes: Short for 'sexual predator' in this context; carries legal and clinical weight that distinguishes it from other terms in this section; zero valorizing connotation; no ambivalence.

definition: A person sexually and/or romantically attracted to people of the opposite sex or gender.
notes: Derived from Greek 'hetero' (other) and Latin 'sexualis'; informal equivalents include 'straight' and 'het'.

definition: A person sexually and/or romantically attracted to people of the same sex.
notes: Clinical term that can feel cold or medicalizing in community contexts; some LGBT individuals perceive it as pejorative when used by outsiders; preferred alternatives include 'gay' and 'lesbian' in most conversational registers.

definition: A person sexually and/or romantically attracted to both men and women, or to people of their own gender and other genders.
notes: Abbreviated 'bi'; the prefix 'bi' (two) is debated as potentially excluding non-binary identities, though the practical definition has broadened in community use; remains the most widely recognized clinical and colloquial term.

definition: A person sexually and/or romantically attracted to others regardless of their sex or gender identity.
notes: Derived from Greek 'pan' (all); distinguishes from bisexual by foregrounding gender-blindness; gained wider visibility alongside increased non-binary awareness from ~2012 onward.

definition: A person who experiences little or no sexual attraction to others.
notes: Often abbreviated 'ace'; distinct from celibacy (behavioral) and aromanticism (lack of romantic attraction); identity formalized by AVEN (Asexual Visibility and Education Network) from ~2001.

definition: A person who experiences sexual attraction only after forming a strong emotional bond with someone.
notes: Coined c. 2006 on AVEN forums; considered part of the asexual spectrum ('grey-ace'); relatively low mainstream recognition outside queer and online communities.

definition: A person who experiences sexual attraction rarely, weakly, or only under specific circumstances; positioned on the spectrum between asexual and fully sexual.
notes: Also spelled 'greysexual'; part of the ace spectrum; abbreviated 'gray-ace'; low mainstream recognition outside asexuality-focused communities.

definition: An umbrella term for non-heterosexual and/or non-cisgender identities; reclaimed from its historical use as a slur.
notes: Originally meant 'strange/odd'; deployed as a slur against LGBT people; actively reclaimed from ~1990 (Queer Nation); still potentially offensive when used by non-LGBT speakers in some contexts; now standard in academic queer theory.

definition: A gender identity that does not fall exclusively within the traditional binary categories of man or woman.
notes: Abbreviated NB or 'enby'; umbrella term for genderqueer, genderfluid, agender, and related identities; entered mainstream discourse significantly after ~2014; legal gender marker recognition in several jurisdictions.

definition: A person whose gender identity aligns with the sex they were assigned at birth.
notes: Derived from Latin 'cis' (on the same side); coined in academic and activist discourse c. 1990s; often abbreviated 'cis'; politically contested in some circles despite functioning as a neutral descriptive complement to 'transgender'.

definition: A person whose gender identity differs from the sex they were assigned at birth.
notes: Preferred over the outdated 'transsexual' in most modern contexts; often abbreviated 'trans'; historically a medicalized term, now widely used as a self-identifier; functions as both adjective and noun.

definition: A person born with sex characteristics (chromosomes, hormones, gonads, or genitalia) that do not fit typical binary definitions of male or female.
notes: Replaced earlier medical term 'hermaphrodite,' now considered offensive; refers to biological variation distinct from gender identity; prevalence estimates range from 0.02% to 1.7% depending on how narrowly the term is defined.

definition: A person, especially a man, who is sexually and/or romantically attracted to people of the same sex; also used as a general umbrella for non-heterosexual identity.
notes: Originally meant 'happy/lighthearted'; adopted as an LGBT self-identifier from ~1960s; now standard across most English dialects; a secondary pejorative meaning 'lame/stupid' represents distinct semantic drift, more common among younger speakers.

definition: A woman who is sexually and/or romantically attracted to other women.
notes: Derived from Lesbos, Greek island home of the poet Sappho; functions as both clinical term and self-identifier; abbreviated 'les' or 'lez,' the latter carrying potential derogatory connotation depending on speaker.
